arxiv-1507-01284.title: Responses to remixing on a social media sharing website
arxiv-1507-01284.creator: Benjamin Mako Hill, Andrés Monroy-Hernández, Kristina R. Olson
arxiv-1507-01284.description: Abstract In this paper we describe the ways participants of the Scratch online community, primarily young people, engage in remixing of each others’ shared animations, games, and interactive projects. In particular, we try to answer the following questions: How do users respond to remixing in a social media environment where remixing is explicitly permitted?

Thanks: ‡ Department of Computer Science, University of Crete, GR–700 13 Heraklion, Greece. Thanks: # Depar
arxiv-2012-13432.creator: Dimitra Antonopoulou #∗, Marina Bitsaki ‡, Georgia Karali †∗
arxiv-2012-13432.description: Abstract . The financial model proposed in this work involves the liquidation process of a portfolio of n n assets through sell or (and) buy orders placed, in a logarithmic scale, at a (vectorial) price x ∈ ℝ n x\in\mathbb{R}^{n} , with volatility.

arxiv-2109-02084.title: (M)SLA e e -Net: Multi-Scale Multi-Level Attention embedded Network for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
arxiv-2109-02084.creator: 1 st Shreshth Saini, 2 nd Geetika Agrawal
arxiv-2109-02084.description: Abstract Segmentation plays a crucial role in diagnosis. Studying the retinal vasculatures from fundus images help identify early signs of many crucial illnesses such as diabetic retinopathy. Due to the varying shape, size, and patterns of retinal vessels, along with artefacts and noises in fundus images, no one-stage method can accurately segment retinal vessels.

arxiv-2111-10912.title: Johnson Coverage Hypothesis: Inapproximability of k k -means and k k -median in ℓ p \ell_{p} -metrics
arxiv-2111-10912.creator: Vincent Cohen-Addad, Karthik C. S, Euiwoong Lee
arxiv-2111-10912.description: Abstract k k - 𝗆𝖾𝖽𝗂𝖺𝗇 \mathsf{median} and k k - 𝗆𝖾𝖺𝗇𝗌 \mathsf{means} are the two most popular objectives for clustering algorithms. Despite intensive effort, a good understanding of the approximability of these objectives, particularly in ℓ p \ell_{p} -metrics, remains a major open problem.

arxiv-2306-17591.title: On the Effects of Quantum Decoherence in a Future Supernova Neutrino Detection
arxiv-2306-17591.creator: Marcos V. dos Santos, Pedro C. de Holanda, Pedro Dedin Neto, Ernesto Kemp
arxiv-2306-17591.description: Abstract Quantum decoherence effects in neutrinos, described by the open quantum systems formalism, serve as a gateway to explore potential new physics, including quantum gravity. Previous research extensively investigated these effects across various neutrino sources, imposing stringent constraints on spontaneous loss of coherence.

arxiv-2310-15804.title: Unstable independence from the categorical point of view Thanks: The first author is supported by the EPSRC grant EP/X018997/1 and the second author is supported by the Grant Agency of the Czech Republic under the grant 22-02964S
arxiv-2310-15804.creator: M. Kamsma and J. Rosický
arxiv-2310-15804.description: Abstract . We give a category-theoretic construction of simple and NSOP 1 -like independence relations in locally finitely presentable categories, and in the more general locally finitely multipresentable categories. We do so by identifying properties of a class of monomorphisms ℳ \mathcal{M} such that the pullback squares consisting of morphisms in ℳ \mathcal{M} form the desired independence relation.

arxiv-2407-18413.title: Simulation of Neural Responses to Classical Music Using Organoid Intelligence Methods
arxiv-2407-18413.creator: Daniel Szelogowski
arxiv-2407-18413.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Daniel Szelogowski. Music is a complex auditory stimulus capable of eliciting significant changes in brain activity, influencing cognitive processes such as memory, attention, and emotional regulation. However, the underlying mechanisms of music-induced cognitive processes remain largely unknown. Organoid intelligence and deep learning models show promise for simulating and analyzing these neural responses to classical music, an area significantly unexplored in computational neuroscience.

arxiv-2408-10818.title: Learning Randomized Algorithms with Transformers
arxiv-2408-10818.creator: Johannes von Oswald, Seijin Kobayashi, Yassir Akram, Angelika Steger
arxiv-2408-10818.description: Abstract Randomization is a powerful tool that endows algorithms with remarkable properties. For instance, randomized algorithms excel in adversarial settings, often surpassing the worst-case performance of deterministic algorithms with large margins. Furthermore, their success probability can be amplified by simple strategies such as repetition and majority voting.

arxiv-2409-19430.title: ‘Simulacrum of Stories’ : Examining Large Language Models as Qualitative Research Participants DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title from your rights confirmation emai; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06 CCS: Human-centered comput
arxiv-2409-19430.creator: Shivani Kapania, William Agnew, Motahhare Eslami, Hoda Heidari, Sarah Fox
arxiv-2409-19430.description: Abstract . The recent excitement around generative models has sparked a wave of proposals suggesting the replacement of human participation and labor in research and development– e.g., through surveys, experiments, and interviews—with synthetic research data generated by large language models (LLMs). We conducted interviews with 19 qualitative researchers to understand their perspectives on this paradigm shift.

arxiv-2504-02984.title: Language Models Guidance with Multi-Aspect-Cueing: A Case Study for Competitor Analysis
arxiv-2504-02984.creator: Amir Hadifar, Christopher Ochs, Arjan Van Ewijk
arxiv-2504-02984.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Amir Hadifar, Christopher Ochs, Arjan Van Ewijk. Competitor analysis is essential in modern business due to the influence of industry rivals on strategic planning. It involves assessing multiple aspects and balancing trade-offs to make informed decisions. Recent Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities to reason about such trade-offs but grapple with inherent limitations such as a lack of knowledge about contemporary or future realities and an incomplete understanding of a market’s competitive landscape.

pmc-10486101.title: Descriptive ethnobotanical studies are needed for the rescue operation of documenting traditional knowledge
pmc-10486101.creator: Łukasz Łuczaj
pmc-10486101.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In this essay, I claim that the primary aim of ethnobiological research is now to document disappearing traditional knowledge. This is an absolute priority due to the rate at which biocultural biodiversity in the world is disappearing.

pmc-11402980.title: Facile synthesis of novel acidic modified magnetic graphene oxide and its application in the green synthesis of pyrimido[4,5-b]quinolines
pmc-11402980.creator: Sarieh Momeni, Ramin Ghorbani-Vaghei
pmc-11402980.description: This study aimed to create an innovative acidic nano catalyst capable of producing pyrimido[4,5-b]quinolines under environmentally friendly conditions. To achieve this objective, 1,3-benzenedisulfonyl amide (BDSA) was immobilized onto the surface of magnetic graphene oxide (GO/Fe3O4@PTRMS@BDSA@SO3H), and its surface was acidified using chlorosulfonic acid.

pmc-11686704.title: What Are These Cysts Doing in My Graft?! A Meta-Analysis on Cystic Occurrence after Autografting and Allografting for Osteochondral Lesions of the Talus
pmc-11686704.creator: Jari Dahmen, Julian Hollander, James J. Butler, Kaj Emanuel, Quinten Rikken, Sjoerd Stufkens, John G. Kennedy, Gino M M.M.J. Kerkhoffs
pmc-11686704.description: Category:Sports; ArthroscopyIntroduction/Purpose:Graft transplantation is a widely used treatment for large osteochondral lesions of the talus. However, cyst formation surrounding the graft is of concern. The primary purpose was to assess and compare cystic occurrence after autografting, allografting and osteoperiosteal grafting for osteochondral lesions of the talus.

pmc-12584890.title: Serological and molecular evidence of respiratory viral mixed infection in sheep and goats
pmc-12584890.creator: Yahia Hassan Ali, Intisar Kamil Saeed, Muaz Magzob Abdellatif, Alaa Mustafa, Hind AbdelMajeed Rikabi, Husham Mohammed AlHassan Attaalfadeel
pmc-12584890.description: Respiratory infections are considered within the major constraints of animal production; viruses are the major causing pathogens. This study aimed to elucidate the prevalence of parainfluenza virus-3 (PIV-3), bovine viral diarrhea virus, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in sheep and goats and the existence of co-infections.

pmc-13179006.title: Impact of COVID-19 on Movement Disorders Patients in the Outpatient Setting
pmc-13179006.creator: Chase Kingsbury, Shaila Ghanekar, Joshua U Hancock, Colyn White, Yayi Zhao, Yangxin Huang, Oliver Flouty, Theresa A Zesiewicz
pmc-13179006.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic may have been the only worldwide infectious outbreak that many patients have experienced in their lifetime. The impact of COVID-19 on patients with chronic neurodegenerative disease, including movement disorders, is largely unknown. Since patients with movement disorders rely heavily on inpatient therapies and are closely followed by their medical team, it would be reasonable to see an increase in stress during a period of prolonged isolation.

pmc-13203415.title: Mitochondria-Associated mRNAs Restore ATP During Oxidative Stress via Cytosolic Translation
pmc-13203415.creator: Dong-Bin Back, Gen Hamanaka, Ji-Hyun Park, Shin Ishikane, Masayoshi Tanaka, Takafumi Nakano, Yoshihiko Nakamura, Kazuhide Hayakawa
pmc-13203415.description: Mitochondrial transplantation has been proposed as a strategy to restore cellular bioenergetics after oxidative injury, but the mechanisms governing ATP recovery remain unclear. Using placental mitochondria, we examined ATP restoration following H2O2-induced oxidative stress. Unmodified mitochondria modestly increased ATP under baseline conditions but failed to restore ATP after injury.

pmc-13295997.title: Why Hide AI Use? Psychological Configurations and Explainable Machine Learning Evidence from Marketing Work
pmc-13295997.creator: Filiz Mizrak, Turhan Karakaya
pmc-13295997.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in marketing work, yet employees who use AI tools may not always disclose AI’s role in producing their outputs. This study examines AI disclosure silence, defined as employees’ intentional withholding of information about the use, role, or contribution of AI tools in work-related outputs after AI has already been used.

(a) In suits against the United States in the United States Court of Federal Claims or in the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit founded on a contract, agreement, or transaction with an executive department.
